audit_scope.description: This audit covers both EL and CL logic for Ethereum Fusaka/Fulu upgrade, including DAS (Data Availability Sampling), block size validation, sparse blobpool networking, and fork activation.

out_of_scope_reasons.Mainnet/Testnet Testing: All testing should be done on local forks of testnet or mainnet
out_of_scope_reasons.Pricing Oracles: Incorrect data supplied by third party oracles (oracle manipulation/flash loan attacks are in-scope)
out_of_scope_reasons.Third-party Smart Contracts: Any testing with third-party systems and applications is prohibited
out_of_scope_reasons.Test Files: Impacts on test files and configuration files unless stated otherwise
out_of_scope_reasons.Centralization Risks: Impacts involving centralization risks are out-of-scope
out_of_scope_reasons.Privileged Access: Impacts caused by attacks requiring access to privileged addresses without additional modifications are out-of-scope

misclassified_entities.reason: Client implementation teams are an organizational/governance entity, not a runtime external entity that sends data into the system. They produce the software but do not interact with it at runtime.
Network operators run nodes but do not constitute an external entity sending data into the system boundary at runtime. They are the system operators.
Core developers are a governance entity involved in EIP scheduling, not a runtime external entity interacting with the protocol.
EIP authors propose protocol changes but do not interact with the system at runtime.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Gossip (CL)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peers sending DataColumnSidecars via gossip subnets. All data is potentially malicious and must be validated (format, inclusion proof, KZG proofs).

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Req/Resp (CL)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers responding to direct column data requests. Response data is untrusted and must pass the same validation as gossip data.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via devp2p (EL Blocks)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers propagating blocks via P2P. Blocks may be oversized or malformed. EIP-7934 block size check must be applied before expensive validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via devp2p eth/71 (EL Blobpool)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth/71 protocol messages (NewPooledTransactionHashes 0x08, GetPooledTransactions 0x09, PooledTransactions 0x10, GetCells 0x12, Cells 0x13)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers sending eth/71 messages for sparse blobpool. All messages are untrusted: cell_mask may be malformed, cell data may be invalid, providers may selectively withhold data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Provider Peer (Sparse Blobpool)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers claiming provider role for blob data. They may selectively withhold cells, return invalid data, or fail noise column checks. Noise-based misbehavior detection is used but not foolproof.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators can propose invalid blocks, withhold blob data, or submit conflicting attestations. All validator-originated data must be validated.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All received DataColumnSidecars must be validated: format check (column index bounds, cell count), commitment inclusion proof against signed block header, and KZG cell proof verification. Invalid sidecars must be rejected and peer may be penalized.
Column data received via Req/Resp must undergo identical validation to gossip-received data. Missing or invalid responses should trigger retry from alternative peers.

RLP-encoded block size must be checked against MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8,388,608 bytes) early in the validation pipeline, before expensive operations like signature verification, to prevent resource exhaustion DoS.

All eth/71 messages must be parsed defensively. cell_mask must be validated as nil when no type-3 transactions are present, or as valid B_16 bitmap otherwise. Message sizes and field counts must be bounds-checked.

Cell data from providers must be validated per EIP-7594 (KZG proofs). Noise column must be checked: if provider fails to return the randomly selected noise column, peer should be flagged for misbehavior. At least 2 distinct providers must be observed before sampling.
Block proposals from validators must be fully validated including signature, state transition, and data availability (DAS sampling must confirm blob data availability before attestation).
